LHH is managing the recruitment and application process for the Director of Operations position on behalf of Eastern Star Church’s ROCK Community Center for Youth and Children (RCCYC).

OUR MISSION

The ROCK Community Center for Youth & Children (RCCYC) champions the development of healthy, whole, and resilient youth and children
in Arlington Woods and beyond. The Center provides safe,
accessible,
high-quality,
holistic
programs
and
support
services
for K–12 youth and their families, spanning education, recreation, leadership, and enrichment.

YOUR ROLE IN OUR MISSION

The Director of Operations
ensures that the day-to-day administrative, logistical, and support functions
of RCCYC run smoothly so staff, volunteers, and youth can thrive in a safe, well-managed environment.

This role manages registration, attendance, food service coordination, transportation liaison activities, supply/inventory control, scheduling, and compliance reporting
. Additionally, the Director of Operations manages operational
budget
lines
(supplies, snacks/meals, transportation, and administrative systems) and provides regular financial updates to the Center Director
, who holds overall responsibility for RCCYC’s budget and grant compliance.

Essential Duties & Responsibilities

Administrative & Enrollment Management

Oversee youth registration, enrollment, and renewal processes; maintain accurate records and databases.
Manage daily attendance tracking and ensure accurate reporting.
Ensure compliance with confidentiality, licensing, and funder requirements for documentation.

Daily Operations & Logistics

Coordinate transportation logistics, including IPS bussing and parent/guardian pick-up protocols.
Oversee snack/meal service in collaboration with the Kitchen Manager.
Maintain inventory of supplies; manage ordering and distribution.
Backup for CACFP reporting and compliance working directly with the Kitchen Manager.
Ensure all classrooms and program spaces are ready for use each day.

Staff Scheduling & Support

Develop and manage daily/weekly staff schedules in collaboration with the Center Director and Director of Programs.
Track staff time, coverage needs, and substitute arrangements.
Support incident documentation and ensure compliance with RCCYC and ESC policies.

Budget & Financial Stewardship

Manage operational budget lines (supplies, food/snacks, transportation, administrative systems).
Monitor daily/weekly expenditures to ensure alignment with approved budgets.
Review monthly financial statements with the Center Director.
Collaborate with the Center Director to plan and adjust budget allocations as needed.

Safety & Compliance Support

Partner with ESC’s central Facilities and Security teams to ensure a safe, welcoming environment.
Maintain compliance with youth protection, health, and safety policies in all operational areas.
Conduct operational checks to identify and resolve risks before they impact programming.

Reporting & Accountability

Provide the Center Director with operational reports (attendance, incidents, meal counts, transportation).
Contribute data for grant reporting, compliance audits, and funder updates.

Supervisory Responsibilities

Administrative Coordinator
Kitchen Manager
Transportation Liaison

Requirements

QUALIFICATIONS:

Required

Bachelor’s degree in business administration, nonprofit management, or related field—or equivalent operational leadership experience.
3+ years of experience in operations, administration, or logistics within a youth-serving or nonprofit environment.
Demonstrated experience managing budgets or budget lines.
Strong organizational, scheduling, and recordkeeping skills.
Ability to work 100% onsite, 9 hours daily (8 hrs onsite + 1 hr lunch).

Preferred

Experience with afterschool, community center, or youth-serving program operations.
Familiarity with grant compliance and reporting.
Bilingual skills a plus.

Certifications/Requirements

CPR/First Aid (or attainable within 60 days).
Mandated Reporter training.
Background check clearance.

Competencies

Operational Excellence – Manages logistics and processes to ensure smooth daily operations.
Financial Stewardship – Manages operational budgets responsibly and transparently.
Organization & Planning – Anticipates needs and prevents disruptions.
Collaboration – Works effectively with Center Director, Programs Director, and ESC teams.
Accountability – Produces accurate, timely reports.
Adaptability – Responds quickly to daily challenges and unexpected changes.

Physical/Work Conditions

Active, youth-centered environment requiring mobility across program areas.
Ability to lift up to 25 lbs. for supplies and equipment.
Daily onsite presence for 8 working hours plus a 1-hour lunch (9-hour workday total).

Success Metrics

Accurate, timely registration and attendance records.
Efficient, uninterrupted daily operations.
Operational budgets tracked and managed responsibly within approved limits.
Compliance with all RCCYC and funder requirements.
Positive staff and family satisfaction with logistics and support systems.

jobs.title: Executive Director
jobs.description:
Bike-Walk Alliance of New Hampshire Seeks Executive Director
Bike-Walk Alliance of New Hampshire (BWANH), the statewide bike-pedestrian advocacy and education organization, has launched its search for a part-time (up to 30 hours per week) Executive Director. Working in a small state where an individual can readily make connections, develop influence, and have an impact, our Executive Director will have the opportunity to use their expertise, organizational skills, and creative talents to their fullest.

BWANH Background

BWANH is a 501(c)(3) non-profit, with its programs conducted by a part-time Executive Director, volunteer board, program-area committees, and other volunteers. Founded in 2004, BWANH is a respected resource for bike-walk safety, education, and advocacy programs throughout New Hampshire, and seeks to enhance its effectiveness in making New Hampshire a safer place for people on bicycles and other vulnerable road users, while providing more opportunities for people to engage in bicycling and other forms of active transportation. The organization works regularly with state and regional agencies, municipalities, and schools, as well as national organizations including League of American Bicyclists and Safe Routes Partnership. BWANH also serves on the NHDOT Bicycle-Pedestrian Transportation Advisory Committee and the DOT’s Complete Streets Advisory Committee. From its office in Concord, BWANH supports other bike-walk groups across the state by providing information, training, resources, fiscal sponsorship, and advocacy support. BWANH has played an important role in advancing active transportation policy in New Hampshire. The organization was instrumental in the 2008 passage of New Hampshire’s “3-Foot-Plus” law and helped defeat HB1703 in 2026, which would have created an annual bicycle registration fee. BWANH continues to work with the Legislature on measures that expand opportunities and protections for people who bike, walk, and use other forms of active transportation. 

Executive Director (ED) Duties and Expectations

Location
: Remote, based in or near New Hampshire, with occasional time in the Concord office and regular travel throughout the state for meetings and events, primarily in the Concord area.

Responsibilities
:
● Work with the Board of Directors to develop and implement annual work plans to achieve strategic goals.
● Work with the Board of Directors to develop and implement a fundraising and development plan to support an enhanced budget that supports the ED and other staff, as well as program expenses.
● Coordinate the development of and supervise the implementation of a communications and marketing plan in consultation with the Board of Directors.
● Develop and manage marketing strategies to increase BWANH’s visibility, supporter engagement, and statewide impact.
● Oversee BWANH’s digital presence, including website content, email newsletters, social media channels, and online supporter engagement.
● Create and manage content for programs, events, advocacy initiatives, fundraising campaigns, and outreach.
● Work with the Board of Directors to revise BWANH’s financial supporter model, with a view to increasing BWANH’s reach and impact.
● Supervise other part-time employees and contractors, which include a bookkeeper and could include an office manager and outreach/communications coordinator.
● Oversee financial operations.
● Oversee organizational tasks such as donor/supporter database, email lists, electronic and hard copy filing, invoicing, and communications with members and the public.
● Establish and maintain relationships with policymakers, the media, the public, partner organizations, sponsors, and community groups.
● Support state-level advocacy efforts, committees, etc.
● Oversee event planning and management, including leading efforts for statewide Bike Month (May) and Pedestrian Safety Month (October) activities.
● Support the Board by working with the president on agendas, ensuring materials are distributed, and ensuring the secretary prepares and submits minutes.
● Support the Board and its committees by attending meetings, helping develop agendas and developing content when necessary

Hours
: The current Executive Director works 30 hours per week and is supported by a contract bookkeeper. In the past, the Executive Director has worked fewer hours with support from a part-time operations manager and communications coordinator. The new Executive Director will have the opportunity to help shape a staffing model that meets both their needs and BWANH’s organizational goals. Depending on the skills and interests of candidates, this position may also be combined with one or both of two related positions. 

Requirements
:
● A self-starter with:
o Strong verbal and written communication skills
o Excellent organizational and interpersonal skills
o Solid computer skills
o Business or non-profit program management experience
o College degree or equivalent

Experience in any of the following areas would be a plus
:
● Experience in public advocacy
● Experience in non-profit fundraising
● Experience in non-profit management
● Experience in public speaking and working with the media
● Experience in public forums, events, providing testimony, etc.
● Organizational skills for planning events
● Passion for bicycling and/or walking, and knowledge of related safety issues.

How to Apply

To apply for the position of Executive Director, please submit a resume and letter of interest, including compensation requirements, by email to BWANH at info@bwanh.org . Position open until filled. Funding is not available for relocation expenses.

Additional Information

Please visit the Bike-Walk Alliance of NH website at www.BWANH.org for additional information including our mission statement, goals, and current Board members. For questions about the Executive Director position, please contact info@bwanh.org .

jobs.title: Chief Operating Officer (COO)
jobs.description:
Job Title

Chief Operating Officer (COO)

Detailed Job Description

Job Overview

The Chief Operating Officer (COO) is responsible for leading the company's overall operational strategy, organizational execution, and day-to-day business operations. As a core member of the executive leadership team, the COO translates corporate strategy into actionable operating plans and ensures that the organization executes its strategic priorities efficiently, consistently, and at scale.

The COO oversees major operational functions across the organization, drives cross-functional coordination, optimizes organizational resources, and establishes performance management systems to improve operational efficiency, customer satisfaction, profitability, and long-term business performance.

The role serves as the central bridge between corporate strategy, organizational execution, operational performance, and business growth, ensuring that the company has the processes, people, systems, and capabilities required to achieve its strategic objectives.

Key Responsibilities
I. Corporate Operations Strategy

Develop and execute the company's overall operational strategy in alignment with corporate vision, business objectives, and long-term growth plans.
Translate the CEO's strategic priorities into clear operational plans, initiatives, milestones, and measurable outcomes.
Establish operating models, organizational structures, governance mechanisms, and performance standards that support scalable growth.
Continuously evaluate the organization's operating model and identify opportunities for improvement.

II. Enterprise-wide Operational Management

Oversee the company's major operational functions and ensure effective coordination across business units and corporate departments.
Monitor day-to-day business operations and ensure that critical processes operate efficiently and consistently.
Establish enterprise-wide operating standards, policies, procedures, and accountability mechanisms.
Ensure operational resources are aligned with strategic priorities and business requirements.

III. Business Performance and KPI Management

Establish and monitor enterprise-wide KPIs covering revenue performance, profitability, productivity, customer satisfaction, operational efficiency, quality, delivery, and organizational performance.
Develop executive dashboards and management reporting systems to provide leadership with timely visibility into business performance.
Identify performance gaps and lead corrective action and improvement initiatives.
Establish a data-driven management culture focused on measurable outcomes and accountability.

IV. Process Optimization and Operational Excellence

Analyze and optimize end-to-end business processes across the organization.
Drive standardization, automation, digitalization, and continuous improvement of core operating processes.
Promote methodologies such as Lean, Six Sigma, Agile, automation, and other operational excellence frameworks where appropriate.
Eliminate organizational silos, reduce operational complexity, and improve decision-making speed and execution efficiency.

V. Cross-functional Coordination

Work closely with Finance, Sales, Marketing, Product, Technology, Human Resources, Legal, Procurement, Customer Success, and other functions.
Establish effective cross-functional collaboration mechanisms and decision-making processes.
Resolve organizational conflicts, operational bottlenecks, and resource allocation issues.
Ensure that different departments work toward common corporate objectives and performance targets.

VI. Financial and Resource Management

Partner with the CFO and executive leadership team to manage operating budgets, cost structures, and resource allocation.
Optimize the use of human resources, technology, facilities, capital, supply chain resources, and other operational assets.
Identify opportunities to improve productivity, reduce unnecessary costs, and increase operating margins.
Ensure operational investments generate measurable business value.

VII. Risk Management, Compliance, and Business Continuity

Establish enterprise-level operational risk management and early-warning mechanisms.
Identify and manage operational, financial, regulatory, technology, supply chain, customer, and reputational risks.
Work with Legal, Compliance, Risk, Security, and Finance teams to strengthen internal controls and governance.
Ensure business continuity, crisis preparedness, and organizational resilience.

VIII. Digital Transformation and Organizational Innovation

Lead enterprise-wide operational transformation and modernization initiatives.
Promote the adoption of digital platforms, automation, artificial intelligence, analytics, and other technologies that improve operational efficiency and scalability.
Partner with CIO, CTO, and technology leadership to align technology investments with business priorities.
Develop innovative operating models that improve organizational agility and responsiveness.

IX. Customer and Service Excellence

Ensure operational processes and organizational capabilities consistently support customer needs and business commitments.
Monitor customer satisfaction, service quality, delivery performance, and operational responsiveness.
Work with Sales, Marketing, Product, Customer Success, and Service teams to improve the end-to-end customer experience.
Establish mechanisms for translating customer feedback into operational and organizational improvements.

X. Leadership and Organizational Development

Build and lead a high-performing executive and operational leadership organization.
Develop senior leaders and functional executives while strengthening organizational capabilities and management depth.
Establish succession planning, leadership development, performance management, and talent development systems.
Promote a culture of accountability, collaboration, operational excellence, innovation, and continuous improvement.

Qualifications
Education Background

Bachelor's degree or above in Business Administration, Operations Management, Engineering, Finance, Economics, Management, or a related field.
MBA, Master's degree, or equivalent advanced qualification preferred.

Work Experience

Typically 18+ years of professional experience in operations, business management, strategy, general management, or related fields, including 10+ years in senior executive leadership positions.

Proven track record of leading large-scale organizations, managing complex operations, and translating corporate strategy into measurable business results.

Strong experience managing multiple business functions, cross-functional teams, large budgets, and geographically distributed operations.

Experience in multinational corporations, high-growth companies, or complex multi-business organizations preferred.

jobs.description:
Chief Operating Officer (Founding Executive) — BlueStar Air Group

Aviation Startup | Founder-Stage Equity: 1%–3% | Salary Upon Funding | Contract Role

BlueStar Air Group
, parent company of the emerging BlueStar Airlines, is building a next-generation U.S. aviation company from the ground up. We are assembling a Founding Executive Team
of senior leaders who will help establish the strategic, operational, financial, and cultural foundation of a new aviation brand.
We are seeking a Chief Operating Officer (Founding Executive)
with significant passenger-airline leadership experience who can transform BlueStar’s vision into a safe, compliant, financially disciplined, and customer-ready operation.
The ideal candidate has previously served as an airline COO, President, CEO, or equivalent enterprise operating executive and understands what it takes to launch, scale, transform, or stabilize complex airline operations.
This is not a co-founder role. It is a Founding Executive
position with meaningful influence, executive responsibility, and equity.
About the Role As Chief Operating Officer, you will serve as the Founder and CEO’s senior operating partner and lead the development of BlueStar’s operational foundation.
You will:
Convert BlueStar’s business plan, funding milestones, operating agreements, and launch objectives into an integrated execution plan.
Build the company’s operating model, decision-making structure, performance standards, readiness gates, and escalation processes.
Help prepare BlueStar’s public-charter operations under 14 CFR Part 380.
Establish effective operating interfaces with BlueStar’s contracted Part 121 direct air carrier.
Oversee BlueStar’s airport, station, ground-handling, vendor, customer-service, and operational-readiness planning.
Support the negotiation and implementation of ACMI and other critical operating agreements.
Develop partner scorecards, service-level expectations, operating metrics, and corrective-action processes.
Establish BlueStar-side emergency response, business continuity, security coordination, irregular-operations, and customer-recovery practices.
Partner with the CFO on operating budgets, startup cash requirements, contract exposure, unit economics, and financial discipline.
Partner with the CHRO on organizational design, executive recruitment, workforce planning, leadership accountability, and culture.
Collaborate with aviation counsel, technology leadership, and flight-operations and certification leaders.
Translate operational requirements into practical technology, data, and AI capabilities.
Represent BlueStar’s operating strategy in investor, Board, airport, vendor, and strategic-partner discussions when authorized.
Build a scalable operating foundation that supports BlueStar’s immediate launch and future Part 121 pathway.

During BlueStar’s initial ACMI/public-charter phase, the contracted certificated direct air carrier will retain operational control and responsibility for the aircraft, crews, maintenance, and certificated flying operation. The COO will lead BlueStar’s enterprise readiness, partner governance, customer delivery, and operational coordination without assuming the certificated carrier’s statutory authority.
Who We’re Looking For We are looking for an executive who:
Has 15 or more years of progressive airline or aviation-operations leadership experience.
Has substantial leadership experience within a U.S. passenger airline.
Possesses deep knowledge of Part 121 airline operations.
Has held a COO, President, CEO, or equivalent enterprise operating position.

Exceptional EVP or SVP airline executives with comparable enterprise-wide responsibility may also be considered.
The successful candidate should also have:
A documented record of launching, scaling, transforming, or stabilizing airline operations.
Experience leading complex, safety-sensitive, multi-function, or multi-station operations.
Strong knowledge of airline safety, regulatory compliance, airport operations, ground handling, security, customer operations, and vendor management.
Experience managing significant operating budgets, service-level agreements, performance dashboards, audits, and corrective-action systems.
Strong crisis-leadership and irregular-operations experience.
The ability to communicate confidently with investors, regulators, airport officials, partners, employees, and executive stakeholders.
The courage to identify and escalate risks—even when doing so is difficult, unpopular, or expensive.
A builder’s mindset and the ability to create structure in an early-stage environment.

Highly Preferred Experience Prior service as an airline COO, President, or CEO.
Public-charter experience under 14 CFR Part 380.
ACMI, wet-lease, charter, or contracted-carrier relationships.
Part 121 certification, certificate transition, or major regulatory-readiness experience.
Safety Management Systems, emergency response, security programs, internal audits, and operational manuals.
Airline startup, turnaround, network expansion, or multi-station growth.
Airline technology, operations-control systems, data governance, analytics, or responsible AI deployment.
Bachelor’s degree or equivalent executive experience. Relevant advanced degrees and aviation credentials are valued but not required.

Leadership Expectations The right COO will be:
A builder
who creates scalable systems from ambiguity.
An operator
who understands the details and makes timely decisions.
A steward
who protects safety, customers, employees, capital, regulatory credibility, and BlueStar’s long-term vision.
A partner
who can challenge respectfully, communicate transparently, and remain aligned with the CEO and executive team.
A people leader
who develops accountable, high-performing teams.

This position requires someone who can think strategically, execute decisively, build responsibly, and help get BlueStar off the runway.

Compensation This is an early-stage Founding Executive
position. Compensation is expected to include:
Founder-stage equity: 1%–3%
, based on experience, scope, involvement, and required approvals.
Future executive salary once funding is secured and the individual transitions into full-time executive employment.
Executive-level influence in building a growing aviation group.
Final equity, vesting, compensation, authority, and employment terms documented in written agreements.

Important This is a pre-launch, funding-contingent opportunity.
The initial arrangement is expected to be a contract role. Transition into salaried executive employment will depend upon funding, approved budget, corporate authorization, and execution of a formal employment agreement.
This is a Founding Executive
role—not a co-founder designation. The title reflects the executive’s opportunity to help build BlueStar during its formative stage. All authority, equity, compensation, vesting, and responsibilities will be governed by the applicable written agreements.
Why Join BlueStar Air Group Build the operating foundation of a new U.S. aviation company.
Work directly with the Founder and CEO.
Help prepare BlueStar for a planned 2027 launch.
Shape the company’s safety culture, operating model, customer experience, and leadership standards.
Help manage major airline, airport, vendor, and strategic partnerships.
Build an organization where safety, service, strategy, stewardship, and scalability grow together.
Join BlueStar at the true ground-floor stage.
Help create something ambitious, meaningful, and capable of changing the aviation industry.

How to Apply Please submit:
Your résumé or executive CV.
A brief statement explaining the most complex airline launch, transformation, turnaround, or expansion you have led.
A summary of your Part 121, Part 380, ACMI, charter, or contracted-carrier experience.
An explanation of why building BlueStar from the ground up is the right next chapter for you.

If you are prepared to turn an aviation vision into a disciplined operating reality, we want to hear from you.
Work Location:
Hybrid remote in Sanford, Florida 32773. Regular executive presence at BlueStar’s Sanford/SFB-area operation and domestic travel will be required as the company approaches launch.

Bike-Walk Alliance of New Hampshire Seeks Executive Director
Bike-Walk Alliance of New Hampshire (BWANH), the statewide bike-pedestrian advocacy and education organization, has launched its search for a part-time (up to 30 hours per week) Executive Director. Working in a small state where an individual can readily make connections, develop influence, and have an impact, our Executive Director will have the opportunity to use their expertise, organizational skills, and creative talents to their fullest.

BWANH Background

BWANH is a 501(c)(3) non-profit, with its programs conducted by a part-time Executive Director, volunteer board, program-area committees, and other volunteers. Founded in 2004, BWANH is a respected resource for bike-walk safety, education, and advocacy programs throughout New Hampshire, and seeks to enhance its effectiveness in making New Hampshire a safer place for people on bicycles and other vulnerable road users, while providing more opportunities for people to engage in bicycling and other forms of active transportation. The organization works regularly with state and regional agencies, municipalities, and schools, as well as national organizations including League of American Bicyclists and Safe Routes Partnership. BWANH also serves on the NHDOT Bicycle-Pedestrian Transportation Advisory Committee and the DOT’s Complete Streets Advisory Committee. From its office in Concord, BWANH supports other bike-walk groups across the state by providing information, training, resources, fiscal sponsorship, and advocacy support. BWANH has played an important role in advancing active transportation policy in New Hampshire. The organization was instrumental in the 2008 passage of New Hampshire’s “3-Foot-Plus” law and helped defeat HB1703 in 2026, which would have created an annual bicycle registration fee. BWANH continues to work with the Legislature on measures that expand opportunities and protections for people who bike, walk, and use other forms of active transportation. 

Executive Director (ED) Duties and Expectations

Location
: Remote, based in or near New Hampshire, with occasional time in the Concord office and regular travel throughout the state for meetings and events, primarily in the Concord area.

Responsibilities
:
● Work with the Board of Directors to develop and implement annual work plans to achieve strategic goals.
● Work with the Board of Directors to develop and implement a fundraising and development plan to support an enhanced budget that supports the ED and other staff, as well as program expenses.
● Coordinate the development of and supervise the implementation of a communications and marketing plan in consultation with the Board of Directors.
● Develop and manage marketing strategies to increase BWANH’s visibility, supporter engagement, and statewide impact.
● Oversee BWANH’s digital presence, including website content, email newsletters, social media channels, and online supporter engagement.
● Create and manage content for programs, events, advocacy initiatives, fundraising campaigns, and outreach.
● Work with the Board of Directors to revise BWANH’s financial supporter model, with a view to increasing BWANH’s reach and impact.
● Supervise other part-time employees and contractors, which include a bookkeeper and could include an office manager and outreach/communications coordinator.
● Oversee financial operations.
● Oversee organizational tasks such as donor/supporter database, email lists, electronic and hard copy filing, invoicing, and communications with members and the public.
● Establish and maintain relationships with policymakers, the media, the public, partner organizations, sponsors, and community groups.
● Support state-level advocacy efforts, committees, etc.
● Oversee event planning and management, including leading efforts for statewide Bike Month (May) and Pedestrian Safety Month (October) activities.
● Support the Board by working with the president on agendas, ensuring materials are distributed, and ensuring the secretary prepares and submits minutes.
● Support the Board and its committees by attending meetings, helping develop agendas and developing content when necessary

Hours
: The current Executive Director works 30 hours per week and is supported by a contract bookkeeper. In the past, the Executive Director has worked fewer hours with support from a part-time operations manager and communications coordinator. The new Executive Director will have the opportunity to help shape a staffing model that meets both their needs and BWANH’s organizational goals. Depending on the skills and interests of candidates, this position may also be combined with one or both of two related positions. 

Requirements
:
● A self-starter with:
o Strong verbal and written communication skills
o Excellent organizational and interpersonal skills
o Solid computer skills
o Business or non-profit program management experience
o College degree or equivalent

Experience in any of the following areas would be a plus
:
● Experience in public advocacy
● Experience in non-profit fundraising
● Experience in non-profit management
● Experience in public speaking and working with the media
● Experience in public forums, events, providing testimony, etc.
● Organizational skills for planning events
● Passion for bicycling and/or walking, and knowledge of related safety issues.

How to Apply

To apply for the position of Executive Director, please submit a resume and letter of interest, including compensation requirements, by email to BWANH at info@bwanh.org . Position open until filled. Funding is not available for relocation expenses.

Additional Information

Please visit the Bike-Walk Alliance of NH website at www.BWANH.org for additional information including our mission statement, goals, and current Board members. For questions about the Executive Director position, please contact info@bwanh.org .

Job Title

Chief Operating Officer (COO)

Detailed Job Description

Job Overview

The Chief Operating Officer (COO) is responsible for leading the company's overall operational strategy, organizational execution, and day-to-day business operations. As a core member of the executive leadership team, the COO translates corporate strategy into actionable operating plans and ensures that the organization executes its strategic priorities efficiently, consistently, and at scale.

The COO oversees major operational functions across the organization, drives cross-functional coordination, optimizes organizational resources, and establishes performance management systems to improve operational efficiency, customer satisfaction, profitability, and long-term business performance.

The role serves as the central bridge between corporate strategy, organizational execution, operational performance, and business growth, ensuring that the company has the processes, people, systems, and capabilities required to achieve its strategic objectives.

Key Responsibilities
I. Corporate Operations Strategy

Develop and execute the company's overall operational strategy in alignment with corporate vision, business objectives, and long-term growth plans.
Translate the CEO's strategic priorities into clear operational plans, initiatives, milestones, and measurable outcomes.
Establish operating models, organizational structures, governance mechanisms, and performance standards that support scalable growth.
Continuously evaluate the organization's operating model and identify opportunities for improvement.

II. Enterprise-wide Operational Management

Oversee the company's major operational functions and ensure effective coordination across business units and corporate departments.
Monitor day-to-day business operations and ensure that critical processes operate efficiently and consistently.
Establish enterprise-wide operating standards, policies, procedures, and accountability mechanisms.
Ensure operational resources are aligned with strategic priorities and business requirements.

III. Business Performance and KPI Management

Establish and monitor enterprise-wide KPIs covering revenue performance, profitability, productivity, customer satisfaction, operational efficiency, quality, delivery, and organizational performance.
Develop executive dashboards and management reporting systems to provide leadership with timely visibility into business performance.
Identify performance gaps and lead corrective action and improvement initiatives.
Establish a data-driven management culture focused on measurable outcomes and accountability.

IV. Process Optimization and Operational Excellence

Analyze and optimize end-to-end business processes across the organization.
Drive standardization, automation, digitalization, and continuous improvement of core operating processes.
Promote methodologies such as Lean, Six Sigma, Agile, automation, and other operational excellence frameworks where appropriate.
Eliminate organizational silos, reduce operational complexity, and improve decision-making speed and execution efficiency.

V. Cross-functional Coordination

Work closely with Finance, Sales, Marketing, Product, Technology, Human Resources, Legal, Procurement, Customer Success, and other functions.
Establish effective cross-functional collaboration mechanisms and decision-making processes.
Resolve organizational conflicts, operational bottlenecks, and resource allocation issues.
Ensure that different departments work toward common corporate objectives and performance targets.

VI. Financial and Resource Management

Partner with the CFO and executive leadership team to manage operating budgets, cost structures, and resource allocation.
Optimize the use of human resources, technology, facilities, capital, supply chain resources, and other operational assets.
Identify opportunities to improve productivity, reduce unnecessary costs, and increase operating margins.
Ensure operational investments generate measurable business value.

VII. Risk Management, Compliance, and Business Continuity

Establish enterprise-level operational risk management and early-warning mechanisms.
Identify and manage operational, financial, regulatory, technology, supply chain, customer, and reputational risks.
Work with Legal, Compliance, Risk, Security, and Finance teams to strengthen internal controls and governance.
Ensure business continuity, crisis preparedness, and organizational resilience.

VIII. Digital Transformation and Organizational Innovation

Lead enterprise-wide operational transformation and modernization initiatives.
Promote the adoption of digital platforms, automation, artificial intelligence, analytics, and other technologies that improve operational efficiency and scalability.
Partner with CIO, CTO, and technology leadership to align technology investments with business priorities.
Develop innovative operating models that improve organizational agility and responsiveness.

IX. Customer and Service Excellence

Ensure operational processes and organizational capabilities consistently support customer needs and business commitments.
Monitor customer satisfaction, service quality, delivery performance, and operational responsiveness.
Work with Sales, Marketing, Product, Customer Success, and Service teams to improve the end-to-end customer experience.
Establish mechanisms for translating customer feedback into operational and organizational improvements.

X. Leadership and Organizational Development

Build and lead a high-performing executive and operational leadership organization.
Develop senior leaders and functional executives while strengthening organizational capabilities and management depth.
Establish succession planning, leadership development, performance management, and talent development systems.
Promote a culture of accountability, collaboration, operational excellence, innovation, and continuous improvement.

Aviation Startup | Founder-Stage Equity: 1%–3% | Salary Upon Funding | Contract Role

BlueStar Air Group
, parent company of the emerging BlueStar Airlines, is building a next-generation U.S. aviation company from the ground up. We are assembling a Founding Executive Team
of senior leaders who will help establish the strategic, operational, financial, and cultural foundation of a new aviation brand.
We are seeking a Chief Operating Officer (Founding Executive)
with significant passenger-airline leadership experience who can transform BlueStar’s vision into a safe, compliant, financially disciplined, and customer-ready operation.
The ideal candidate has previously served as an airline COO, President, CEO, or equivalent enterprise operating executive and understands what it takes to launch, scale, transform, or stabilize complex airline operations.
This is not a co-founder role. It is a Founding Executive
position with meaningful influence, executive responsibility, and equity.
About the Role As Chief Operating Officer, you will serve as the Founder and CEO’s senior operating partner and lead the development of BlueStar’s operational foundation.
You will:
Convert BlueStar’s business plan, funding milestones, operating agreements, and launch objectives into an integrated execution plan.
Build the company’s operating model, decision-making structure, performance standards, readiness gates, and escalation processes.
Help prepare BlueStar’s public-charter operations under 14 CFR Part 380.
Establish effective operating interfaces with BlueStar’s contracted Part 121 direct air carrier.
Oversee BlueStar’s airport, station, ground-handling, vendor, customer-service, and operational-readiness planning.
Support the negotiation and implementation of ACMI and other critical operating agreements.
Develop partner scorecards, service-level expectations, operating metrics, and corrective-action processes.
Establish BlueStar-side emergency response, business continuity, security coordination, irregular-operations, and customer-recovery practices.
Partner with the CFO on operating budgets, startup cash requirements, contract exposure, unit economics, and financial discipline.
Partner with the CHRO on organizational design, executive recruitment, workforce planning, leadership accountability, and culture.
Collaborate with aviation counsel, technology leadership, and flight-operations and certification leaders.
Translate operational requirements into practical technology, data, and AI capabilities.
Represent BlueStar’s operating strategy in investor, Board, airport, vendor, and strategic-partner discussions when authorized.
Build a scalable operating foundation that supports BlueStar’s immediate launch and future Part 121 pathway.

During BlueStar’s initial ACMI/public-charter phase, the contracted certificated direct air carrier will retain operational control and responsibility for the aircraft, crews, maintenance, and certificated flying operation. The COO will lead BlueStar’s enterprise readiness, partner governance, customer delivery, and operational coordination without assuming the certificated carrier’s statutory authority.
Who We’re Looking For We are looking for an executive who:
Has 15 or more years of progressive airline or aviation-operations leadership experience.
Has substantial leadership experience within a U.S. passenger airline.
Possesses deep knowledge of Part 121 airline operations.
Has held a COO, President, CEO, or equivalent enterprise operating position.

Exceptional EVP or SVP airline executives with comparable enterprise-wide responsibility may also be considered.
The successful candidate should also have:
A documented record of launching, scaling, transforming, or stabilizing airline operations.
Experience leading complex, safety-sensitive, multi-function, or multi-station operations.
Strong knowledge of airline safety, regulatory compliance, airport operations, ground handling, security, customer operations, and vendor management.
Experience managing significant operating budgets, service-level agreements, performance dashboards, audits, and corrective-action systems.
Strong crisis-leadership and irregular-operations experience.
The ability to communicate confidently with investors, regulators, airport officials, partners, employees, and executive stakeholders.
The courage to identify and escalate risks—even when doing so is difficult, unpopular, or expensive.
A builder’s mindset and the ability to create structure in an early-stage environment.

Public-charter experience under 14 CFR Part 380.
ACMI, wet-lease, charter, or contracted-carrier relationships.
Part 121 certification, certificate transition, or major regulatory-readiness experience.
Safety Management Systems, emergency response, security programs, internal audits, and operational manuals.
Airline startup, turnaround, network expansion, or multi-station growth.
Airline technology, operations-control systems, data governance, analytics, or responsible AI deployment.
Bachelor’s degree or equivalent executive experience. Relevant advanced degrees and aviation credentials are valued but not required.

Leadership Expectations The right COO will be:
A builder
who creates scalable systems from ambiguity.
An operator
who understands the details and makes timely decisions.
A steward
who protects safety, customers, employees, capital, regulatory credibility, and BlueStar’s long-term vision.
A partner
who can challenge respectfully, communicate transparently, and remain aligned with the CEO and executive team.
A people leader
who develops accountable, high-performing teams.

This position requires someone who can think strategically, execute decisively, build responsibly, and help get BlueStar off the runway.

position. Compensation is expected to include:
Founder-stage equity: 1%–3%
, based on experience, scope, involvement, and required approvals.

Executive-level influence in building a growing aviation group.

About Stack Trading

Stack Trading is a technology-first proprietary trading firm based in Frisco, Texas. We are fundamentally disrupting the retail prop trading landscape. We do not operate simulation casinos or rely on B-book traps (trailing drawdowns, consistency) to fail traders. Instead, we offer a transparent, premium evaluation process featuring static drawdowns, algorithmic trading, market data depth,  Tier-1 institutional liquidity, and a W2 career pipeline for traders who prove their edge.

The Role

We are seeking a highly connected Senior Director of Partnerships to lead our B2B acquisition strategy.
You are a hunter. Your sole mandate is to identify, negotiate with, and close the largest trading educators, Discord operators, and financial influencers in the prop trading industry. Armed with an industry-disrupting multi-tier affiliate program and massive absolute dollar payouts, you will systematically migrate top-tier networks away from our competitors and onto the Stack Trading platform.

This is a high-autonomy, high-visibility role for a closer who knows the proprietary trading landscape inside and out.

What You Will Do

Leverage Your Rolodex:
Capitalize on your existing relationships within the retail trading space to immediately build a high-converting B2B pipeline.
Close Enterprise Partners:
Pitch our institutional infrastructure, W2 trader pipeline, and lucrative Master Override structures to secure high-volume partners.
Strategic Deal-Making:
Manage complex, 30 to 60 day sales cycles from initial discovery to contract execution. Utilize a dedicated travel and entertainment budget to close deals face to face.
Revenue Generation:
Build and manage a multi-million dollar book of business, collaborating directly with our executive team to continually optimize our go-to-market enterprise pitch.

Who You Are

Experienced:
5 to 10+ years of B2B sales, business development, or partnership experience directly within the proprietary trading space. We are conducting a nationwide search for exact industry experience and connections.
Connected:
You possess an active, verified network of high-net-worth trading educators, community managers, or financial influencers.
Industry Fluent:
You have a deep understanding of affiliate marketing economics, CPA/CAC metrics, and retail trading platforms (Futures and Spot Forex).
A Closer:
You know that securing enterprise partnerships requires active listening, relationship building, and solving the partner's specific pain points. You excel at establishing the deep trust necessary to secure a signature and transition an affiliate’s network.
Mobile:
Willingness to travel up to 30% domestically and internationally for high-value client acquisition.

Uncapped OTE:
$250,000 - $300,000+
Commission Structure:
Aggressive percentage of gross revenue generated by your book of business, heavily incentivized by volume accelerators and flat enterprise-tier bonuses.
Benefits:
Comprehensive Health, Dental, and Vision coverage.
Resources:
T&E budget for strategic client entertainment and travel.
